description: The Sprites REPORTERS half, and the name now says what the fixture pins: `new_turtle`/`who`/`turtles` are reserved WITHOUT the Sprites profile. All three `define`s raise `ol-reserved-word` under `["core-language", "turtle-rendering"]` — Sprites is the profile that owns these names and it is NOT claimed, which is the whole point; Turtle & Rendering is present only because Sprites depends on it in the profile DAG and this fixture sits in the Sprites tree. Keeping reporters separate from the block-heads (`reserved-procedures-without-sprites`) is deliberate: they reach the built-in-names predicate as registered PRIMITIVES rather than as keywords, so a change that fixed one category and missed the other would still turn this fixture red. HISTORY: issue #746 wrote it as the OFF half of a profile gate, expecting three clean declarations; `spec/grammar.md:408` and ruling #833 retracted that gate, and issue #841 removed it from the checker -- the expectation is flipped rather than the fixture deleted, so the behaviour stays pinned across the reversal. `"check": true`: checker diagnostics only, nothing executes. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below, and the asymmetry with the twin is intentional rather than an oversight: the harness does not compare `message` even when a fixture supplies it (measured -- a deliberately wrong `message` here still passed the suite), so including it would add an assertion nothing verifies. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:253`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. Dropping the decorative `message` from the twins is a corpus-wide edit and belongs to issue #842.
